steps.note: S4.1.6 states the net target change $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$ independent of the initial scratch values $a,c$, with S4.1.5 giving the first rows cancelling the old effect and the last two rows restoring the scratch values, as at 744-750.
S4.1.7 gives the bit-case central coefficient $|S\cap T|\bmod2$, the side injection cancelling exactly the intersection-one cases, intersections zero or two already zero, and self coefficient one.
S4.1.8 gives the complex central coefficient $(|S\cap T|-1)/2$ with the side wires cancelling it for intersections zero and two and intersection one contributing zero, matching 756-758.
S4.1.9 states the three stages $(x,y)\to(x,y+x)\to(-y,y+x)\to(-y,x)$ with every invocation restoring its own scratch wires.

The plan asserts every edge joins comparable labels (S4.3.4) and names tabulating the orthogonal residual of every edge in a method, but gives only the gate-label table (S4.3.4.1) and the residuals of the side edge $2\to5$ and center edge $3\to4$, not the per-edge residual table with dimensions of lines 1022-1043.
S4.3.4.2 states $t_X\perp t_Y$ gives $\langle t_X\rangle\subset t_Y^\perp$, so the labels nest, with residual $P\otimes\langle t_X,t_Y\rangle^\perp$ of dimension $h-2$.
S4.3.4.3 makes center $3\to4$ the only decreasing edge losing $h$ ($L=Ich$) and S4.3.4.4 telescopes at gates to sources $N$, sinks $Wm-N$, signed $Wm-2N$, absolute adding $2L$.

S4.3.4.5 states that over $\mathbb F_2$ every nonzero residual is nondegenerate and nonalternating (it contains a coordinate unit of norm one), hence has an orthonormal basis; the plane-absorption argument of 1087-1102 is not spelled out but the defining claim and its reason are.
S4.3.5 states $L_{\rm b}/N=100/539$ and $L_{\rm c}/N=101/539$, quoting line 1107.

S4.3.7.3 gives weight additivity mod 4 for orthogonal binary vectors and S4.3.7.4 the formula $q_V-q_U=\sum_{v\in\mathcal B}\operatorname{wt}(v)[v\cdot x]$ over an orthonormal basis of the residual, negated on decreasing edges.

S4.3.7.4 notes $\operatorname{wt}(v)$ is odd and S4.3.7.5 writes $i^{\varepsilon[v\cdot x]}$ as a combination of $1$ and $(-1)^{v\cdot x}$, turned by $H\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)H=X$ into $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse.

S4.3.7 and S4.3.7.2 give one kernel per residual basis vector with $s_{\rm c}$ in all, and S4.6.1.4/S4.6.1.7 state that on $f$ columns each residual basis vector gives one tensored factor $(C^{\epsilon_h})^{\otimes f}$, $s_{\rm c}$ child calls in all, as the paper uses it at 1878-1906.

S4.3.7.6 gives $C^{-1}$ on the 27 coordinates of $\operatorname{supp}(u_a)$ repaired by $Z_{a,k}$ before and $i^{27k}Z_{a,k}$ after via $C=iZC^{-1}Z$, and S4.3.7.7 negates the $X$ outputs so every role carries $C^{\otimes m}$; the frames $I$ and $C^{\otimes m}$ of the zero and full labels are only implicit in that conclusion.
S4.3.5 states both loss ratios are below $1/2$ so a strict saving remains, and S4.3.6.2/S4.3.7.2 give $s<Wm$ with deficit $N-2L_{\rm b}$ and $2N-2L_{\rm c}>0$.
S4.4.1-S4.4.4 state both deficits exceed $20\cdot2^{-50}$, $\log m<20$, $m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20\cdot2^{-50})>m(1-\eta)$, hence $s/W<m^\tau$ with $\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}$.

S4.5.1.2 gives the pivot at the topmost nonzero row's rightmost entry, clearing left and below by lower-triangular elementary operations, deleting the pivot row and column and repeating, and S4.5.1.1 that $\Pi$ has exactly $a$ ones.
S4.5.1.3 states a fixed odd prime avoiding all denominators and diagonal numerators of a finite table so the identities specialize to $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$ with invertible triangular factors.
S4.5.1.4 states a lower triangular transformation costs $O(V)$ by updating coordinates in descending physical order with a diagonal unit and earlier coordinates.
S4.5.1.5 gives $D_j\gets D_j+H_i$, interchange, $D_j\gets H_i-D_j$ yielding $(h+d,d)$ with one interchange per one of $\Pi$, $a$ in all.
S4.6.4.5 states $A(e)\le sA(e/m)+E$ at an internal node and $A(e)\le8e$ at a leaf, and S4.6.4.3-S4.6.4.4 derive the per-invocation count $24W^3+4s+4W+4<E$.

S4.6.4.8 states depth-$\ell$ values lie in $2^{-(p+\ell)}\mathbb Z[i]$ with modulus at most $2^\ell$ so $p+\Delta$ fractional and $\Delta+3$ integer bits are exact, and S4.6.4.9 that $\epsilon C_1<1$ gives $\Delta=o(p)$.
S4.6.5.6 states every row of $\mathcal H$ has absolute row sum one, so disks are preserved, and truncation errs by less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$.

summary: P04 states 25 of 26 sub-steps, nearly all as explicit infer steps quoting the cited lines: the bank-exchange network (B1-B4), the side-edge nesting, decreasing-edge telescoping, binary orthonormal bases and loss ratios (L2-L5), the phase interface (P1-P4, with the k-column factorization stated in the butterfly-layer steps), the rank deficits and exponent (R1-R4), the matrix shear (M1-M4) and the simultaneous-layer depth and precision bounds (S1-S5). The only absence is L1: the plan gives the gate-label table and two edge residuals but not the per-edge orthogonal residual table with dimensions.
